items.label: Abaxent
items.title: A broker that works for the buyer
items.summary: Abaxent has brokered technology in Wisconsin for 22 years, and the old site read like one more reseller. The new one opens on a single question, what's a broker, then answers it with a four-step method, 93% partner retention and the three people who run it.

items.label: NAMC 2027
items.title: One question on the first screen: attend, sponsor or exhibit
items.summary: The forum site buried the schedule, the map and the sponsor levels behind buttons. The 2027 conference site opens by asking what you're here to do, then puts the $400 ticket, six sponsor levels and the $1,500 booth one click away.

items.label: Milo's Cafe

shots.alt: Milo's Cafe home page with the storefront and the headline A little Europe, a lot of flavor
Milo's Cafe patio scene in the morning with a time-of-day slider

items.title: A café site with a patio that follows the sky
items.summary: People looking up Milo's want the menu, the prices and whether the patio is worth it today. The site answers all three on one page, with a patio drawn from the real Morrisville sky and a little glass that pours on every drink.

items.label: NLT BKNY

shots.alt: New Life Tabernacle home page with the headline we believe God.
A word for today: a list of feelings beside a verse from Scripture

items.title: A church site the staff can run
items.summary: Service times, video, events and giving for a Brooklyn church, with an email sign-in so the staff update it themselves.

items.label: Summit
items.title: Turning discovery notes into a plan
items.summary: Shopify discovery ends in a pile of notes. Summit turns them into requirements, risks, a roadmap and a QA plan, and the landing page shows what comes out.

items.label: Iron Clad
items.title: A live odds terminal
items.summary: A sports analytics site for MLB, NFL, NBA, NHL and WNBA. It shows current market prices and ranks three daily parlays by probability and value, with a plain-English reason for each pick.

items.label: happy's

shots.alt: happy's home page: a wall of smiley faces behind the headline come by, feel good
happy's walk-up page: the upstairs cocktail bar behind a staircase

items.title: A bar site that looks like the bar
items.summary: The smiley wall, a sticker-style menu and a staircase you can climb, for a cocktail bar in downtown Cary.

items.label: The WalkUp
items.note: Concept site, not a launched project

shots.alt: The WalkUp home page: exposed brick behind the headline A little above the usual
The WalkUp menu: tabs for cocktails, beer, wine and snacks, with prices

items.title: A bar that's easy to find, one flight up
items.summary: A seasonal menu with glasses that pour, the room in real photos, and a clear way upstairs, for the bar above happy's.
